title: 2nd Mystery The Equality Of Few And Many Through The Mystery Of Luminosity And Obedience

questions.question: What is the main idea of the Second Mystery in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah can do many things as easily as one thing, and big things are no harder for Him than small things.

questions.question: What example is given from light to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: One sun can show its light in many mirrors and shiny drops at the same time.

questions.question: In that example, what does the sun give besides light?
questions.answer: It also gives warmth.

questions.question: What example is used about sound and hearing?
questions.answer: One word can be heard by one person and also by many people.

questions.question: What does that sound example teach about Divine power?
questions.answer: It shows that reaching many is not harder than reaching one.

questions.question: Which created being is named as an example of a luminous spirit?
questions.answer: Gabriel.

questions.question: What is said about Gabriel or a spirit like him?
questions.answer: Such a being can be in many places or look toward many places with Allah’s power.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes this wide-reaching activity possible?
questions.answer: Allah’s command, power, and mercy make it possible.

questions.question: What comparison is made between great and small?
questions.answer: They are the same for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What comparison is made between many and few?
questions.answer: They are also the same for Allah’s power.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk about mirrors, ears, and spirit beings?
questions.answer: It uses them as examples to explain a hard idea in a simple way.

questions.question: In the first example, what happens when light reaches many reflecting surfaces?
questions.answer: The same light appears in all of them.

questions.question: In the second example, what happens to one spoken word?
questions.answer: It can reach one ear or many ears.

questions.question: What point is being made by that example?
questions.answer: A single action can affect many without extra difficulty.

questions.question: In the third example, what can a luminous spirit do?
questions.answer: It can be present in many places, or direct its attention to many places.

questions.question: Is this ability described as coming from the spirit by itself?
questions.answer: No. It happens by Allah’s power and permission.

questions.question: Which two pairs are directly compared in the passage?
questions.answer: Great and small, and many and few.

questions.question: What is the result of those comparisons?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that for Allah’s power, these differences do not create difficulty.

questions.question: What can we infer about Allah from this passage?
questions.answer: His power is unlimited and not restricted the way human ability is.

questions.question: What is the title of the target passage?
questions.answer: The Second Mystery.

questions.question: What three ideas are mentioned at the start to explain this mystery?
questions.answer: Brightness, clearness, and obedience.

questions.question: How does the passage use the sun as an example?
questions.answer: It says one sun can appear in many reflecting things at once.

questions.question: Why is the sun example helpful?
questions.answer: It gives a picture of how one source can affect many receivers together.

questions.question: What role does Divine command have in the passage?
questions.answer: It is one of the reasons this wide activity happens easily.

questions.question: What role does boundless creativity have in the example of the spoken word?
questions.answer: It shows that one act can spread to very many places without strain.

questions.question: What everyday human example is used so kids can picture the idea more easily?
questions.answer: A single word entering ears.

questions.question: How is Gabriel used in the explanation?
questions.answer: Gabriel is given as an example of a luminous spirit that can relate to many places.

questions.question: What repeated message comes at the end of both paragraphs?
questions.answer: There is no difference between one and many, or between large and small, for Allah’s power.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly about human strength or Allah’s strength?
questions.answer: It is about Allah’s strength and power.

questions.question: What kinds of things receive the sun’s reflection in the passage?
questions.answer: Mirrors, bright objects, and drops of water.

questions.question: What does it mean that big and small are alike in this example?
questions.answer: It means both can receive the reflection, so size does not matter.

questions.question: What simple action is used next after the light example?
questions.answer: Hearing one spoken word.

questions.question: How many hearers can receive that one word according to the passage?
questions.answer: It can be heard by one person or by a huge number of people.

questions.question: What does this suggest about reaching many listeners?
questions.answer: It does not make the action harder in the way we might expect.

questions.question: What can such a being do by Divine power?
questions.answer: It can be in many places or direct itself to many places at once.

questions.question: What phrase best captures the message about numbers?
questions.answer: Few and many are the same for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What phrase best captures the message about size?
questions.answer: Small and great are the same for Allah’s power.

questions.question: What important belief about Allah is supported by these examples?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfect and unlimited.

questions.question: What does the passage want the reader to understand about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: That Allah can carry out many actions easily and completely.

questions.question: Which natural object is the first teaching example?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: What does the sun do in the example?
questions.answer: It appears with its brightness and warmth in many reflectors.

questions.question: Why is that example important for understanding the main point?
questions.answer: It shows how one source can reach countless receivers at the same time.

questions.question: What human experience is used as the next example?
questions.answer: Speaking one word and it being heard.

questions.question: How does that human example connect to the main idea?
questions.answer: It shows that one thing can go to many places without becoming divided in a weak way.

questions.question: Who is named to show an example from the unseen world?
questions.answer: Gabriel.

questions.question: What is said about his relation to many places?
questions.answer: He can be present in or turn toward many places by Allah’s power.

questions.question: What is the same in all three examples?
questions.answer: In each one, a single source reaches many places or receivers.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from these examples?
questions.answer: For Allah, dealing with one or many makes no difference.

questions.question: Does the passage present Allah’s power as narrow or vast?
questions.answer: Vast and unrestricted.

questions.question: What topic is explained in the target passage?
questions.answer: It explains a mystery about how Allah’s power works with perfect ease.

questions.question: What qualities are mentioned before the sun example begins?
questions.answer: Brightness, clearness, and obedience.

questions.question: In the first paragraph, what shows that one source can affect countless things?
questions.answer: The sun’s reflection appearing in many different reflecting surfaces.

questions.question: Besides mirrors, what other things are mentioned that can reflect light?
questions.answer: Shiny objects and droplets.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the difference between large and small in this matter?
questions.answer: It says there is no difference.

questions.question: In the second paragraph, what is the first comparison?
questions.answer: One spoken word reaching one ear or many ears.

questions.question: What does this example help us infer about Divine creativity?
questions.answer: It is so wide and great that reaching many does not make it difficult.

questions.question: After the example of the spoken word, what two examples are given of single luminous beings?
questions.answer: An eye-like light and a spirit being such as Gabriel.

questions.question: What can they do through Divine power?
questions.answer: They can be in many places, look toward many places, or enter many places.

questions.question: What word in the passage shows that this happens only by Allah’s allowance?
questions.answer: Permission.

questions.question: What is repeated to make the point very clear?
questions.answer: That one and many, and small and great, are alike for Allah’s power.

questions.question: If you had to explain this passage to a classmate in one sentence, what would you say?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is so complete that doing many things is just as easy for Him as doing one thing.
